We need correlate OTDR events with link record.

Link record route km from site A:
A-ODF 0.0
SC-01 3.877
SC-02 8.6
SC-03 10.723
SC-04 12.986
B-ODF 14.82

OTDR from A distances are fibre distances from ODF at shooting site with launch/receive cords 1 km used. Note says distances are fibre distances from ODF at shooting site. Launch and receive cords of 1.000 km were used; receive cord ends in open connector.

The OTDR from A: event 1 at -0.0 reflective loss 0.21. Event 2 at 3.956 km non-reflective loss 0.04. That's close to SC-01 at 3.877 km. Good.

Event 3 at 8.781 km non-reflective loss 0.74. SC-02 at 8.6 km. Slight offset due to fibre excess? 8.781 vs 8.6 reasonable.

Event 4 at 10.989 km non-reflective loss 1.29 dB. SC-03 is at 10.723 km. Close. Loss 1.29 dB is high for a splice closure. Typical splice loss maybe 0.04-0.1 per splice. 1.29 dB is abnormal. Also timing matches SC-03 re-entered 2026-10-24 06:52 UTC for branch addition, and alarm raised 2026-10-24 08:00 UTC. So likely bad splice at SC-03.

Event 5 at 13.347 km non-reflective loss 0.07. SC-04 at 12.986 km. Slightly offset.

Event 6 at 15.232 km reflective loss 0.21. That's B-ODF? Wait B-ODF at 14.82 km route. Fibre distance maybe longer due to slack. 15.232 km reflective likely B-ODF connector.

Event 7 at 16.232 km end.

OTDR from B: distances from B ODF. Should see mirror.

From B, distance 0.001 reflective. That's B-ODF.

Event 2 at 1.888 km non-reflective loss -0.05. That's maybe SC-04? Let's compute distance from B: route distance from B to SC-04 = 14.82 -12.986 = 1.834 km. Close to 1.888 km. Loss -0.05 (gain?) maybe measurement noise.

Event 3 at 4.243 km non-reflective loss 1.33 dB. Distance from B to SC-03 = 14.82 -10.723 = 4.097 km. Close to 4.243 km. Loss 1.33 dB matches 1.29 dB from A side. So confirms loss at SC-03.

Event 4 at 6.448 km non-reflective loss -0.64. Distance from B to SC-02 = 14.82 -8.6 =6.22 km. Close to 6.448. Loss negative maybe measurement.

So fault is at SC-03 with ~1.3 dB excess loss. Could be bad splice.

Also performance: RX power drop ~1.3 dB, matches OTDR loss increase ~1.29 dB. TX stable. BER degraded.

Site notes: SC-03 re-entered 2026-10-24 06:52 UTC to add branch. So likely splice bad.

Check if could be macrobend? Macrobend typically shows gradual loss and OTDR shows dip. Event loss 1.29 dB at a point ~10.989 km, corresponds to SC-03 at 10.723 km. Could be bad splice.

Fault type options: dirty_connector, damaged_connector, macrobend, bad_splice, fibre_break, wrong_attenuator, tx_degradation.

Bad splice fits. Element_id SC-03. Action resplice.

Need to ensure single root cause. Could also be wrong attenuator? B-ATT design 10 dB. Could be changed? No evidence. TX stable. Connector at B ODF cleaned 2026-10-18. So not dirty.

The OTDR event at SC-03 is non-reflective loss 1.29 dB. From A side 10.989 km. From B side 4.243 km loss 1.33 dB. Consistent.

We should also compute expected link loss. Commissioning loss 3.39 dB @1550. TX 1.55 dBm avg, B-ATT 10 dB, RX expected = TX - link_loss - attenuator? Wait attenuator at B between ODF and receiver. So RX power = TX - fibre loss - connector losses - attenuator. Commissioning loss 3.39 dB is A-ODF to B-ODF. So expected RX = TX -3.39 -10 = 1.55 -13.39 = -11.84 dBm. Actual before fault ~ -12.1 avg, close. After fault ~ -13.4 avg, difference ~1.3 dB, matches.

So diagnosis: bad_splice at SC-03, action resplice.
